title: The Other Captain

stages.title: Report to Arcadia Station
stages.journal: Hegemony customs flagged your identity: a revenue officer at Arcadia Station wants a word about "outstanding obligations".
stages.nextStep: Report to the revenue office at Arcadia Station

stages.title: Back taxes
stages.journal: The revenue officer is out with his fleet. He will find you.

stages.title: The paper trail
stages.journal: Someone has been running up debts in your name. The Hegemony records office at Arcadia Station keeps the paper trail.
stages.nextStep: Visit the records office at Arcadia Station

stages.title: The Foundling Wheel
stages.journal: Your "donations" go to the Foundling Wheel, an orphanage station at Nomios. Its charity gala is hosted by its generous patron: you. Allegedly.

stages.title: Before the gala
stages.journal: The Foundling Wheel's charity gala is in a week. $toc_starsector_name, wearing your name, will be there.

stages.title: The gala
stages.journal: The Foundling Wheel's charity gala is tonight. So is $toc_starsector_name.
stages.nextStep: Attend the gala at the Foundling Wheel

stages.title: After the gala
stages.journal: $toc_starsector_firstName got away, and the Foundling Wheel's reactor was failing behind you.

stages.title: The search
stages.journal: $toc_starsector_firstName got away. The Hegemony is looking; so are you.

stages.title: The reckoning
stages.journal: $toc_starsector_name is hiding at Agreus, in Arcadia.

nodes.title: Customs
nodes.text:
The docking clamps engage, then disengage, then engage again, as if the station can't decide whether to let you in.

A customs officer appears on your comm, reading from a screen. "$playerName? Your identity is flagged for outstanding obligations to the Hegemony Revenue Service. Fees, fines, a tax or two." He squints. "Several taxes. Please report to the revenue office at Arcadia Station at your earliest convenience."

"Or at our convenience," he adds. "Which comes sooner."

options.text: Say there must be a mistake
Promise to report to Arcadia Station

nodes.text: "Everybody says that." He doesn't look up. "Arcadia Station. Revenue office. Have a pleasant day, $playerSirOrMadam."

options.text: Sigh, and plot a course to Arcadia

nodes.arriveText: Arcadia Station's revenue office keeps a light on for you. Literally: your name is blinking on the board above the counter.

nodes.title: Revenue office
nodes.text:
The clerk checks the board, then you, then the board again. "Revenue Officer $toc_varro_name handles your file personally. He's out with his fleet." She taps a key. "I've let him know you're here. He'll meet you when you undock."

"Most people try to leave," she adds kindly. "It never helps."

options.text: Undock and get it over with

nodes.title: Back taxes
nodes.text:
$toc_main_a1_after_v1

You spend the next hour going through the documents Varro sent. The signatures are yours. The handwriting isn't. The ship registrations are yours, except for the ships, which you have never owned. Someone has been living your life, and doing it badly.

options.text: Find out who is using your name

cases.text: Ten thousand credits lighter, you watch the Hegemony fleet form up and leave. Varro waves. You don't.
Varro's fleet leaves with a polite apology and an even more polite reminder that the debt is still on file.
The Hegemony fleet limps away, and somewhere a revenue officer is filing a report with the word "assault" in it, several times.

phrases.otherwise: You never let the tax collector catch you. By now, a report with your name on it is on its way to every Hegemony office in the sector.

ops.text: You talked your way out of the debt
You ran from the tax collector

nodes.arriveText: The records office at Arcadia Station is three floors of filing cabinets and one very tired archivist.

nodes.title: Records office
nodes.text:
The archivist pulls your file. It is thick. It is much thicker than your life.

Credit lines, ship leases, a gambling debt on Chicomoztoc, and a standing monthly donation to the Foundling Wheel Charity Fund, an orphanage station at Nomios. Every withdrawal from that fund is signed by its generous patron: "Capt. $playerName".

Pinned to the back of the file, a flyer: the Foundling Wheel's charity gala, hosted by the same generous patron. There is a picture. It is not you.

options.text: Ask who that is in the picture
Take copies of everything

nodes.text:
The archivist runs the face. The match comes back in under a second, which, she says, is a record. "$toc_starsector_name. Identity theft, tax evasion, three counts of accidental arson, one of deliberate arson, and..." she scrolls, "...stealing from orphans. Wanted in four systems. $toc_He owes more than you do, and you owe a lot."

"Well. $toc_He owes it as you."

options.text: Take copies of everything

nodes.arriveText: The Foundling Wheel turns slowly over Nomios, patched in six colours. A banner across the docking ring reads WELCOME TO OUR PATRON, with your name spelled correctly. Small mercies.

nodes.title: The Foundling Wheel
nodes.text:
Two children are waiting at the airlock with a hand-painted sign. The taller one, $toc_orr_name, holds it upside down. The smaller one, $toc_phan_name, corrects it, then looks you up and down.

"You're shorter than on the poster," says $toc_phan_name.
"And you came early," says $toc_orr_name. "The gala's not for a week. Are you checking on the fund? Matron says you check on the fund a lot."

options.text: Play along, and ask them to show you around
Tell them you are not who they think you are
Ask them to fetch an adult

nodes.text:
They show you everything: the hydroponics bay, the classroom, the reactor room they are absolutely not allowed in. $toc_orr_name explains how the coolant pumps work, in detail, twice. By the end of it they are holding your hands.

"See you at the gala, Captain," says $toc_phan_name. "Bring the real cake this time."

options.text: Promise to come to the gala

nodes.text:
They listen to the whole story. $toc_orr_name looks crushed. $toc_phan_name looks thoughtful, then disappears and comes back with a crumpled receipt.

"The patron dropped this last time. I kept it because the signature looked wrong. You do your Ps differently." She hands it over. "If that's not you, who is it?"

options.text: Take the receipt, and promise to find out at the gala

nodes.text:
$toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name exchange a look, the look children give adults who have just failed a test. They fetch the matron, who is polite, busy and no help at all.

On your way out you hear $toc_phan_name: "Told you the poster was nicer."

options.text: Leave, and come back for the gala

nodes.title: The gala
nodes.text: An invitation pings your comm, addressed to you, signed by you: the Foundling Wheel's charity gala starts tonight.

options.text: Plot a course to Nomios

nodes.arriveText: The Foundling Wheel is lit up like a festival. Shuttles from three systems crowd the docking ring.

nodes.title: The gala bar
nodes.text:
The gala starts at the bar, the way the best ones do. Somebody has hung bunting from the coolant pipes. Every few minutes a guest raises a glass "to Captain $playerName, the most generous captain in the sector!" and the bar cheers. Nobody looks at you. Nobody knows your face. They know your name very well.

$toc_main_gala_bar_v1

options.text: Chat with the guest who keeps toasting you
Go into the hall for the patron's speech

cases.text: $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name are working the bar as volunteer waiters, in bow ties three sizes too big. $toc_phan_name slides you a drink. "On the house," she whispers. "You paid for it. Allegedly."
$toc_phan_name squeezes past with a tray of glasses and hisses, "Is the fake here?" $toc_orr_name, behind her, is glaring at every jacket in the room.
$toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name are serving drinks. They serve everybody near you, and somehow never you.

phrases.otherwise: $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name are serving drinks in bow ties three sizes too big.

repeat.text: The bar is still toasting your name. Through the doors, the hall is filling up for the speech.

nodes.text:
The guest is a cheerful freight broker who has given the Foundling Wheel a great deal of money. "Such a hands-on patron," she beams. "Do you know, the Captain inspected the reactor room personally this afternoon? Alone, for an hour. Very thorough. Such dedication."

You find that you have put your drink down.

options.text: Excuse yourself

nodes.title: The charity gala
nodes.text:
The hall is under the Wheel's old observation dome, packed to the walls. On a stage made of shipping crates, a $toc_man in a very good jacket is giving a speech. "...and that is why I, Captain $playerName, have always believed in giving back." $toc_He has your name, and none of your manners. $toc_He is, you have to admit, a good speaker.

$toc_main_gala_v1

Then $toc_he presses something in $toc_his pocket. The lights die. Security doors slam open all over the station, and a klaxon starts: REACTOR COOLANT FAILURE. In the red light you see $toc_starsector_name running for the hangar with the fund's credit chip in $toc_his teeth.

options.text: Save the Wheel - get to the reactor room
Chase $toc_starsector_firstName down - your name is not leaving with $toc_him

cases.text: $toc_phan_name, at the front, is glaring at $toc_him with her arms crossed. $toc_orr_name is taking notes.
Near the stage, $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name are clapping for $toc_him. They don't look at you.

phrases.otherwise: $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name wave at you from the front row, then at $toc_him, confused.

nodes.title: The reactor room
nodes.text:
$toc_main_save_v1

The klaxon stops. The lights come back. Somewhere far away, a shuttle you will never catch jumps out of the system.

On the reactor room floor, where $toc_starsector_firstName must have planted $toc_his device, lies the Wheel's real fund ledger. Every credit $toc_he took, in $toc_his own handwriting.

options.text: Take the ledger

cases.text: $toc_orr_name gets there before you, shouting the coolant pump routine he explained to you twice. You were listening. Between the three of you, the pumps come back one by one.

phrases.otherwise: You find the reactor room on your third try. $toc_orr_name is already there, shouting the coolant routine at no one in particular. He doesn't like you, but he lets you hold the wrench.

nodes.text: In the morning, $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name are waiting at your airlock with their bags packed. "Matron says we can go with you," says $toc_phan_name, "if you promise to bring us back for school." $toc_orr_name is already asking your engineer about your coolant pumps.

options.text: Welcome them aboard

nodes.title: The hangar
nodes.text:
You reach the hangar as $toc_starsector_firstName's shuttle clears the doors. $toc_He salutes you through the canopy. With your hand, somehow.

In the bay where it stood: a dropped datapad, still logged in. Fuel receipts, a docking reservation at Agreus, and a note: "Remember: be YOU."

Behind you, the Wheel shudders.

options.text: Grab the datapad and run for your ship

ops.text: You chased $toc_starsector_firstName while the Foundling Wheel burned

nodes.title: News from Nomios
nodes.text:
The news reaches you a day later. The Foundling Wheel's reactor went critical an hour after you left. Everyone was evacuated; nobody was hurt, which, given $toc_starsector_firstName, counts as a miracle.

The last shuttle out carried $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name, and their famous patron, Captain $playerName, who had come back for them. $toc_starsector_firstName came back for them. They went with $toc_him.

options.text: Follow the datapad to Agreus

nodes.title: A lead
nodes.text: A message from Arcadia Station, from $toc_varro_name: "Someone using your name, has rented a berth at Agreus. Please don't make me file anything else." There is a smiley at the end. It looks like it was added under protest.

options.text: Head for Agreus

nodes.arriveText: Agreus's docks smell of fuel and bad decisions. Somewhere down here is somebody with your name.

nodes.title: $toc_starsector_name
nodes.text:
$toc_He is in the back of a dockside bar, under a poster of $toc_himself. Of you. $toc_He waves you over like an old friend.

"Captain! Sit, sit. I've been you for three years; it's nice to finally meet me." $toc_main_confront_v1

"Let's be adults about this. I took a name nobody was using properly. You can't prove much. And you don't want a scene."

options.text: Tell Orr and Phan who really destroyed the Wheel
Hand $toc_him over to the Hegemony, with the evidence
options.tooltip: Uses one piece of evidence. Clears your name.

options.text: Hear $toc_his deal
Let $toc_him go
Let Orr and Phan decide
Grab $toc_him - $toc_his fleet can try to stop you

cases.text: $toc_He glances at $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name behind you. "And you brought the kids. Low blow, Captain."
$toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name sit at $toc_his table, eating $toc_his chips. They look at you like you're the one who blew up their home.

nodes.speaker: toc_starsector

nodes.text:
You tell them about the device, the coolant, the credit chip in $toc_his teeth. $toc_orr_name looks at $toc_starsector_firstName. $toc_starsector_firstName looks at the ceiling. $toc_phan_name puts down the chips, slowly, and comes to stand next to you.

"$toc_He said the reactor was an accident," says $toc_orr_name. "$toc_He says everything is an accident."

options.text: Turn back to $toc_starsector_firstName

nodes.text: You tell them everything. They listen politely, the way you once listened to them, and then $toc_phan_name says, "The poster was nicer," and goes back to her chips.

options.text: Turn back to $toc_starsector_firstName

nodes.text: "One hundred thousand credits," $toc_starsector_firstName says, "and I retire your name. Never use it again. I'll be someone else entirely. I was thinking: Admiral." $toc_He slides a credit chip across the table. It is the Wheel's.

options.text: Take the deal
Push the chip back

nodes.text:
$toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name confer in whispers. It takes a while. $toc_starsector_firstName tries to join in and is shushed.

"$toc_He goes to the Hegemony," $toc_phan_name announces at last. "But $toc_he has to write to us. Every week. Real letters."
"With the right handwriting," adds $toc_orr_name.

options.text: Call the Hegemony

nodes.text: $toc_starsector_firstName is out of $toc_his chair before you are, and out of the bar before your crew is. Twenty minutes later $toc_his little fleet is burning hard for the jump point. Your sensors officer asks, quietly, whether "$toc_starsector_firstName's Getaway" is a real fleet name.

options.text: Run $toc_him down

nodes.title: The bounty board
nodes.text: Back on Arcadia Station, the bounty board updates itself with a cheerful chime.

options.text: Read on

nodes.title: The bounty board
nodes.text: Back on Arcadia Station, the bounty board still shows that face. Under your name.

options.text: Read on

nodes.title: What became of everyone
nodes.text:
$toc_main_epilogue_v1

$toc_main_epilogue_v2

$toc_main_epilogue_v3

$toc_main_epilogue_v4

options.text: Close the file

cases.text: The Foundling Wheel still turns over Nomios. Its new coolant pumps carry a small brass plaque with your name on it. Your real name, this time.

phrases.otherwise: Where the Foundling Wheel used to turn, the Nomios traffic charts now show a hazard marker and a slowly spreading debris field. The orphans were rehoused on Nomios. The matron sends a card every year.

cases.text: $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name travel with your fleet now. $toc_orr_name has rewired the coffee machine twice; $toc_phan_name keeps the books, and the books have never been so honest.

With $toc_starsector_firstName in a cell, $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name went back to Nomios. They write to $toc_him every week. They write to you too, less often, with spelling mistakes on purpose.

With $toc_starsector_firstName in a cell, $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name went back to Nomios. They write to $toc_him every week. They write to you too, less often, with spelling mistakes on purpose.

phrases.otherwise: $toc_orr_name and $toc_phan_name left with $toc_starsector_firstName. Postcards arrive from places that don't have post offices.

cases.text: $toc_starsector_name is serving eleven years in a Hegemony penal colony, where $toc_he has already been elected to the prisoners' council under somebody else's name.
$toc_starsector_name was pulled from the wreck of $toc_his flagship, alive and complaining. $toc_He is serving eleven years in a Hegemony penal colony and has opened a gift shop.
$toc_starsector_name writes to the Foundling kids every week from a Hegemony cell. Real letters. The handwriting is $toc_his own.
$toc_starsector_firstName kept $toc_his word, more or less. $toc_He never uses your name again. $toc_He uses your first officer's.

phrases.otherwise: $toc_starsector_name is still out there. Every few months a bill arrives for something you never bought, and a thank-you card for buying it.

cases.text: Your name is clean. The warrant is closed, and $toc_varro_name sent a fruit basket. It came with an invoice.

phrases.otherwise: The warrant is still open. $toc_varro_name at Arcadia Station will take more evidence, one piece at a time, until your name is clean.

notes: Filled in for the user (S10–S16, 2026-11-24). Flags: $global.toc_a1_way (pay, bluff, flee, fight), toc_orphans_trust (kind, honest, rude), toc_orphans_with (player, john), toc_ending (handover, force, deal, letgo, orphans), toc_wheel_saved, toc_name_cleared, toc_john_free.
